newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan agency raids nuclear firm after false report.
newsitem.headline: Japan agency raids nuclear firm after false report.

text.p: Japanese government inspectors raided a nuclear fuel reprocessing company on Wednesday after executives admitted falsifying a report about the country's worst nuclear accident.

A spokesman for the Science and Technology Agency said four officials of the agency's Nuclear Safety Department were inspecting the offices of the Power Reactor and Nuclear Fuel Development Corp (PNC).
A March 11 explosion at a PNC bituminisation plant, designed to harden low-level nuclear waste by mixing it with asphalt, exposed 37 workers to small levels radiation.

The plant is located at Tokaimura, on the Pacific coast just 160 km (100 miles) northeast from Tokyo. The PNC said an initial small fire had not been put out properly and probably caused the explosion nearly nine hours later.
PNC officials told a news conference late on Tuesday that the firm had written a false official report which said staff at the plant had confirmed that a fire there had been put out.
"In fact no one had confirmed that the fire was put out," a PNC spokesman told the news conference.
